sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: CXCL12-AF647 binding to NLuc-hACKR3 membranes confirmed by NanoBRET; VUF16840 and VUF15485 displaced CXCL12-AF647 in a concentration-dependent manner, demonstrating intact ligand-binding function.
sites.rationale: The NLuc tag is explicitly described as N-terminal on full-length hACKR3 expressed in membranes. The NanoBRET assay with fluorescent CXCL12 confirms both membrane/surface display and preserved chemokine-binding function. The N-terminus (residues 1–45) is extracellular per topology landmarks, placing the NLuc tag on the cell surface. Full-length hACKR3 with N-terminal NLuc tag expressed in membranes; CXCL12-AF647 binding to NLuc-hACKR3-expressing membranes quantified by NanoBRET binding assay.

sources.claim: Binding of fluorescent Alexa Fluor 647-labeled CXCL12 (CXCL12-AF647) to membranes expressing N-terminally NLuc-tagged hACKR3 was quantified by a homogeneous NanoBRET binding assay, 40 whereas binding of [ 3 H] VUF15485 to HA-tagged hACKR3 expressing membranes was determined after filtration of incubation mixtures and scintillation counting. 23 Coincubation of CXCL12-A647 and increasing concentrations of VUF16840 or the high-affinity small-molecule ACKR3 agonist VUF15485 23 resulted in a concentration-dependent decrease in CXCL12-A647 binding to membranes expressing the NLuc-hACKR3 ( Fig. 1 A).
To this aim, we added a Flag epitope to the N-terminus of ACKR3 and ACKR3-Venus, and labeled the receptors at 37 °C with Flag antibody conjugated to a fluorphore (M1-Alexa-647).
The construct bore a hemagglutinin signal peptide followed by a Flag-tag preceding the receptor sequence.
Stable HEK293 expressing SNAP-tagged ACKR3 were kindly provided by Meritxel Canals from University of Nottingham.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Used in cell-based assays; specific surface expression or functional assay results not described in this clip.
sites.rationale: The construct explicitly uses residues 2–362 of ACKR3 with an N-terminal FLAG tag, placing the FLAG before D2 (canonical residue 2) in the expressed protein. In canonical numbering this is insert_after_residue=1 (between M1 and D2); Python confirms seq[0]='M' and seq[1]='D'. The N-terminal region (residues 1–45) is extracellular, so this junction is on the cell surface. This is a distinct junction from the prepend-before-M1 sites above. Full-length ACKR3 (residues 2–362) in pcDNA3.1 with N-terminal FLAG tag and C-terminal RlucII fusion (ACKR3_rlucII); used in cell-based assays.

sources.claim: For cell-based assays, ACKR3 (residues 2–362) or CXCR4 (residues 2–352) were inserted into pcDNA3.1 expression vector with an N-terminal FLAG tag and followed with a C-terminal Renilla luciferase II (ACKR3_rlucII and CXCR4_rlucII).

literature_notes: All five ledger lines supporting surface tag sites converge on the extracellular N-terminus of ACKR3 (residues 1–45). No ledger line supports an internal extracellular loop (ECL1 103–119, ECL2 181–209, ECL3 275–295) tag insertion. L2 (Venus at C-tail) and the C-terminal RlucII in L3 are intracellular and recorded in other_positions. The ACKR3 N-terminal extracellular domain contains three cysteines (C21, C26, C34) that may form disulfide bonds and potential N-glycosylation sequons (N13, N22, N39); a prepended tag at position 0 avoids all of these. L3 pins a slightly different junction (insert_after_residue=1, after M1) because the construct uses residues 2–362; this is reported as a distinct site. L6 (SNAP-tag) is topology_derived because the clip names no residue.

literature_other_positions.note: Venus-GFP fused to the C-tail of full-length ACKR3; the C-terminus (residues 319–362) is intracellular per topology landmarks.
C-terminal Renilla luciferase II (RlucII) fusion on full-length ACKR3 (residues 2–362); C-terminus is intracellular per topology landmarks.
